title: Learning to Compress: Unlocking the Potential of Large Language Models for Text Representation
subcategory: context-compression pretext task for unsupervised LLM adaptation, then contrastive learning
task: General-purpose text embeddings from decoder LLMs (clustering, retrieval, STS, classification, reranking)
problem: Causal LLMs are optimised for next-token prediction and token-level pretext tasks (e.g. MNTP in LLM2Vec) are suboptimal for holistic text representations.
architecture: LLM2Comp: compression pre-training in which the LLM produces memory tokens that replace the context for downstream prediction (best objective: KL-based context-token knowledge distillation), followed by unsupervised (dropout) and supervised contrastive learning.

datasets.name: MTEB (subset)
datasets.details: Biorxiv/Medrxiv/TwentyNewsgroups clustering, SciFact/NFCorpus/ArguAna retrieval, STS17/SICK-R/STSB, Banking77/Emotion classification, reranking

key_results: After supervised contrastive learning, LLM2CompKL averages 66.78 with 0.36M training samples vs 66.11 for LLM2Vec with 1.16M samples.
strengths: Sample-efficient adaptation of LLMs to embeddings.
Analysis of effective dimensionality and dimensional collapse.

limitations.text: Retrieval performance declines when contrastive learning continues beyond about 200 steps.
Comparisons with models using other backbones/data are only indicative.
